mcqs.q: Teratogenesis refers to:
opts: Structural or functional defects in the developing embryo/fetus
mcqs.explain: Teratogenesis is structural/functional defects in the embryo or fetus; it also includes growth retardation, fetal death and transplacental carcinogenesis.

mcqs.q: During the first 0–8 weeks (implantation stage), a teratogen may cause:
opts: Abortion, no effect, or an anatomic defect
mcqs.explain: In the 0–8 week (pre/post-implantation) period a teratogen may cause abortion, no effect, an anatomic defect, or a later-detected functional defect.

mcqs.q: Congenital abnormalities account for about ___ of newborn/infant deaths, mostly:
mcqs.explain: Congenital abnormalities comprise about 1/5 of newborn/infant fatalities; the largest portion is cardiac, then lung and chromosomal.

mcqs.q: FDA pregnancy risk category A means:
opts: No fetal risk shown in controlled human studies
mcqs.explain: Category A: no fetal risk demonstrated in controlled human studies in any trimester (the safest).

mcqs.q: FDA category X drugs are those in which:
opts: The risk to the fetus clearly outweighs any benefit — they must be avoided
There is no risk at all
Risk is acceptable in all trimesters
mcqs.explain: Category X: the fetal risk clearly outweighs benefit, so these drugs (e.g. thalidomide) are contraindicated.

mcqs.q: A category D drug is one where:
opts: Human fetal risk exists, but use may be acceptable despite the risk
mcqs.explain: Category D: studies show human fetal risk, but use may still be acceptable when the benefit justifies it (e.g. warfarin, ACE inhibitors).

mcqs.q: Thalidomide (category X) classically causes:
mcqs.explain: Thalidomide is a category X teratogen causing limb (phocomelia) defects and other congenital anomalies.

mcqs.q: High-dose aminoglycosides during pregnancy can damage the:
mcqs.explain: Aminoglycosides (category C) at high dose can cause cranial nerve VIII (vestibulocochlear) damage — fetal ototoxicity/deafness.

mcqs.q: ACE inhibitors in pregnancy are associated with:
opts: Renal tubular dysplasia, skull and pulmonary hypoplasia
mcqs.explain: ACE inhibitors (category D) cause renal tubular dysplasia, skull and pulmonary hypoplasia.

mcqs.q: Which statement about dental treatment in pregnancy is TRUE?
opts: Preventive, diagnostic and restorative treatment is safe throughout pregnancy
All dental treatment must be delayed until after delivery
Local anaesthesia must never be used
mcqs.explain: Preventive, diagnostic and restorative care (including root canals/restorations) is safe throughout pregnancy; delaying may worsen problems.

mcqs.q: Which local anaesthetic is considered SAFE (preferred) in pregnancy?
mcqs.explain: Lidocaine and prilocaine are safe; mepivacaine and bupivacaine are used with caution (fetal bradycardia).

mcqs.q: Tetracycline is AVOIDED in pregnancy because it causes:
mcqs.explain: Tetracycline is contraindicated — it causes discolouration of the developing teeth (and is deposited in bone).

mcqs.q: The analgesic of CHOICE in pregnancy is:
mcqs.explain: Acetaminophen is the safe analgesic of choice; aspirin and other NSAIDs are avoided, especially in the third trimester.

mcqs.q: Aspirin and NSAIDs are avoided (especially in the 3rd trimester) because of:
opts: Postpartum haemorrhage risk (and effects on the fetal circulation)
mcqs.explain: Aspirin is associated with postpartum haemorrhage; NSAIDs are avoided late in pregnancy due to effects on the fetal circulation.

mcqs.q: Nitrous oxide in dentistry should be avoided in which period of pregnancy?
opts: It is never safe at any time
mcqs.explain: Nitrous oxide is avoided in the first trimester (associated with spontaneous abortions); pregnant staff exposure must also be controlled.

mcqs.q: Benzodiazepines are avoided in pregnancy because of an association with:
mcqs.explain: Benzodiazepines are linked to cleft lip/palate, so they are avoided in pregnancy.

mcqs.q: Mepivacaine and bupivacaine are used with CAUTION in pregnancy because they can cause:
mcqs.explain: Mepivacaine and bupivacaine are associated with fetal bradycardia, so they are used cautiously; lidocaine is preferred.

mcqs.q: Pregnant dental personnel need special protection from occupational exposure to:
mcqs.explain: Pregnant dental staff require special consideration regarding direct exposure to nitrous oxide and radiation.

mcqs.q: Chloramphenicol is contraindicated in pregnancy because of:
mcqs.explain: Chloramphenicol is associated with maternal toxicity and fetal death, so it is avoided.

mcqs.q: Which antibiotic is a SAFE first choice in pregnancy?
mcqs.explain: Penicillins (amoxicillin), metronidazole, erythromycin and cephalosporins are safe; tetracycline and chloramphenicol are avoided.

mcqs.q: Which antifungal is safe in pregnancy?
mcqs.explain: Clotrimazole and nystatin are safe; fluconazole and ketoconazole are used with caution (ketoconazole = fetal toxicity).

mcqs.q: Warfarin in pregnancy (category D) can cause:
opts: Skeletal abnormalities (spinal curvature) and limb abnormalities
mcqs.explain: Warfarin is a category D teratogen causing skeletal abnormalities (curvature of the spine) and limb abnormalities.

saqs.q: Define teratogenesis and outline the two developmental stages of risk.
saqs.a: Teratogenesis = structural/functional fetal defects. 0–8 weeks (implantation): abortion, no effect, or anatomic defect. 9 weeks–birth (fetal): growth, neurologic and functional effects.

saqs.q: List the FDA pregnancy risk categories A–X.
saqs.a: A no human risk, B animal risk unconfirmed, C animal risk/no human data, D human risk (may use), X risk outweighs benefit (avoid).

saqs.q: Match each teratogen to its defect: thalidomide, warfarin, aminoglycosides, ACE inhibitors.
saqs.a: Thalidomide → limb defects; warfarin → skeletal/limb; aminoglycosides → CN VIII (deafness); ACE inhibitors → renal/skull/lung hypoplasia.

saqs.q: Which dental analgesics are safe vs avoided in pregnancy?
saqs.a: Safe: acetaminophen (paracetamol). Avoid: aspirin and NSAIDs (especially 3rd trimester) — postpartum haemorrhage.

saqs.q: Which antibiotics are avoided in pregnancy and why?
saqs.a: Tetracycline (tooth discolouration), chloramphenicol (maternal toxicity/fetal death); high-dose gentamicin = fetal ototoxicity.

saqs.q: Is dental treatment safe in pregnancy, and which local anaesthetic is preferred?
saqs.a: Yes — preventive, diagnostic and restorative treatment (incl. root canals) is safe throughout pregnancy. Preferred LA = lidocaine (with epinephrine).

saqs.q: Which sedatives are problematic in pregnancy and how?
saqs.a: Nitrous oxide — avoid 1st trimester (spontaneous abortion); benzodiazepines — avoid (cleft lip/palate). Protect staff from N₂O/radiation.
